desktop.heading: Implementation patterns from the examples.
hero: Each entry connects a problem to the example code that addresses it. Browse by problem here, or follow the build guide in implementation order.

sections.heading: Architecture & composition
intro: Decide what the shell owns, what a component may touch, and which work must stay outside the app.

rules.title: Treat the server as an optional decorator
rules.rule: A peer-to-peer app may use a relay for durability, but it should not need one to start.

rules.title: One shared core, two runtimes
rules.rule: Keep the shared core portable by connecting to the same document from the BEAM and the browser.

rules.title: Keep latency-critical loops out of the update path
rules.rule: Let a real-time loop read a plain snapshot. Do not make it wait on the application.

rules.title: Hand a rendering surface to FFI, and bootstrap on Connected
rules.rule: Let an FFI module own the canvas pixels, and create shared channels only after the connection opens.

rules.title: Stamp the schema; refuse bad reads
rules.rule: Fill and stamp a typed map before attaching it, so an incompatible reader gets an error.

rules.title: Panels take a TypedMap, never a root
rules.rule: Give a reusable component a typed map, whether that map is a root or a child. Keep document-wide effects in the shell.

sections.heading: Conflicts & consistency
intro: Two clients change the same state at once. Keep the UI honest while the shared structure settles the result.

rules.title: Propose on release, render the pending signoff
rules.rule: Send one consensus proposal per gesture, then show whose approval is still missing.

rules.title: Fallible edits render; never assert on a mutation
rules.rule: Handle every index-based edit as fallible. A peer may change the list between render and click.

rules.title: When a move is not atomic, crown one channel authoritative
rules.rule: A move across channels is not atomic. Choose one source of truth and reconcile the rest while rendering.

rules.title: Seed idempotently with Claims
rules.rule: Let every client seed the same initial values through first-writer-wins claims.

rules.title: Anchors, not offsets
rules.rule: Store an anchor instead of a text offset, then resolve its current position after each edit.

rules.title: Show writes that have not settled
rules.rule: When writes are not optimistic, show them as pending until the confirming event arrives.

sections.heading: Presence & coordination
intro: Some facts belong to the session, not the document: who's here, who drives, and what they need to tell each other.

rules.title: The minimal presence idiom
rules.rule: Declare one presence effect, use one typed payload, and remove the local session before the roster enters your model.

rules.title: Ride an application protocol on ripples
rules.rule: Send short-lived coordination over ripples, not through a document channel.

sections.heading: Testing & diagnostics
intro: Reproduce the failures that matter, and read the runtime's own diagnostics before you guess at a sync bug.

rules.title: Sample diagnostics on every event
rules.rule: Put the runtime's diagnostics on screen before you debug synchronization.

rules.title: Extract pure modules; test without a server
rules.rule: Move decisions into pure modules so most tests need no document, sluice, or server.

rules.title: Test client death deterministically
rules.rule: Test a client dying mid-job with an in-process disconnect that produces the same leave event as the server.

desktop.boundary: Copy the constraint, not the whole design. The examples show lifecycle and ownership constraints, not boilerplate to copy whole. Reuse those rules; keep domain-specific state and views close to the app that needs them. Choose an example to trace →
